LABEL: Bolivia
NOTES: MANY OFFICIAL LANGUAGES – The 2009 Constitution of the Plurinational State of Bolivia,
archived on October 24, 2017 in the Internet Archive, establishes multiple official languages.
Article 5 recognizes Spanish, as well as all languages of the indigenous nations and peoples, as official.
The Constitution explicitly lists: Aymara, Araona, Baure, Bésiro, Canichana, Cavineño, Cayubaba, Chácobo,
Chimán, Ese Ejja, Guarani, Guarasu'we, Guarayu, Itonama, Leco, Machajuyai-Kallawaya, Machineri, Maropa,
Mojeño-Trinitario, Mojeño-Ignaciano, Moré, Mosetén, Movima, Pacawara, Puquina, Quechua, Sirionó, Tacana,
Tapiete, Toromona, Uru-Chipaya, Weenhayek, Yaminawa, Yuki, Yuracaré, and Zamuco.
https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Bolivia_2009.pdf?lang=en
https://web.archive.org/web/20171024024514/http://www.harmonywithnatureun.org/content/documents/152Bolivia%20Constitution.pdf

LABEL: Israel
NOTES: Since 2018, Hebrew is the sole official language of Israel.
Arabic holds a special status under the Basic Law, and continues to be used in official documents,
education, and public life for the Arab minority.

LABEL: India
NOTES: [languages]
India does not have a national language. Hindi and English are official languages at the federal level.
22 languages are officially recognized in the Constitution's Eighth Schedule.
Indian Sign Language (ins) is standardized and supported by ISLRTC, though not yet de jure official.

LABEL: British Indian Ocean Territory
NOTES: [languages] The British Indian Ocean Territory has no permanent civilian population.
English is used as the official language for administrative purposes.
No local or sign languages are in use on the territory.

LABEL: Iraq
NOTES: [languages]
Arabic and Kurdish are co-official languages under Article 4 of the 2005 Iraqi Constitution.
Turkmen, Syriac, and Armenian are recognized for official use in administrative units where they are
widely spoken.

LABEL: Iceland
NOTES: [languages] Icelandic Sign Language is legally recognized since 2011 but has no distinct ISO 639-3 code.
Polish is the most spoken foreign language in Iceland due to immigration.

LABEL: Japan
NOTES: [languages]
Japanese is not constitutionally declared official, but functions as the de facto national language.
Ryukyuan and Ainu are indigenous languages with limited speakers and cultural protection.
Japanese Sign Language (JSL) is used and promoted, but lacks ISO recognition.

LABEL: Kenya
NOTES: [languages]
English and Swahili are co-official languages of Kenya (Constitution, Article 7).
Over 60 languages are spoken in Kenya, with Kikuyu, Luo, Kamba and Kalenjin among the most widespread.
Kenyan Sign Language (ksl) is used in education and communication by the deaf community.

LABEL: Kyrgyzstan
NOTES: [languages] Kirghiz is the State language as defined by the Constitution.
Russian is an official language for interethnic communication, widely used in administration and education.

LABEL: Mexico
NOTES: [languages] Mexico recognizes 68 indigenous languages as national languages per LGDLPI (2003),
with official status in the regions where spoken. Only Spanish has nationwide functional official status.

LABEL: Malaysia
NOTES: [languages] Malaysia recognizes Malay (zsm) as the only official language according to Article 152 of
the Constitution. English, Mandarin Chinese (zho), and Tamil (tam) are widely used in education, media,
and commerce. Indigenous groups and migrant communities speak various local languages including
Telugu (tel), Banjar (bjn), Temiar (tem), and others.
[languages] The Malay language also has a different alphabet called 'Jawi', which does not have a
corresponding ISO 639 code. IGNORED.

LABEL: Mozambique
NOTES: [languages] Portuguese is the only official language. Bantu languages are widely used in local communities.
[languages] Makhuwa, Sena, and Tswa-related languages are the most spoken native languages across regions.

LABEL: Namibia
NOTES: [languages] English is the only official language. Afrikaans and Khoekhoe are widely spoken and used
regionally.
[languages] Herero, German, and Lozi have strong presence. Indigenous San languages are spoken by local
groups.

LABEL: New Caledonia
NOTES: [languages] French is the only official language. Kanak languages like Ajië and Drehu are
used in local education.
[languages] Over 30 Kanak languages are recognized as heritage. Several have ISO codes and
active speakers.
[languages] Hmong Njua (hnj) is spoken by a Lao Hmong community in Bourail, active since 1975.

[mottos] Motto 'Inasmuch' is in Norfuk. No ISO code exists, so stored using key 'und' in mottos.official.

LABEL: Romania
NOTES: [languages] Romanian is the only official language. Hungarian (hun) is widely spoken regionally.
[languages] Several minority languages are used locally: Romani, German, Ukrainian, Serbian, Rusyn, etc.

LABEL: Serbia
NOTES: [languages] Serbian (srp) is the only official language. Hungarian (hun) is widely spoken in Vojvodina.
[languages] Minority languages with ISO codes are used locally: Romani, Slovak, Rusyn, Croatian, etc.
